label: Constitutional Analysis
sentences: The question here falls under Article I, Section 1. The lawmaking powers the Constitution grants are given to Congress, which is a Senate and a House. It reads: “All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.”
This story is about an operational ground stop from a communications failure.
In 1787, article I, Section 1 of the Constitution, signed September 17, 1787, says "All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States."

Article I, Section 8, Clause 18 of the Constitution, signed September 17, 1787, lets Congress make the laws needed to carry out powers vested in the Government of the United States "or in any Department or Officer thereof."
The FAA terminated the nationwide ground stop after that failure.
The strongest argument against this is that the agency only carried out safety duties already set by statute, and ending the stop was ordinary work under existing law, not new lawmaking.
We read this clause to mean all granted lawmaking power stays with Congress alone.
We read this clause to mean an agency may regulate only inside what a statute already allows.
Keeping this power with Congress keeps the people in charge.
